A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe-FedLLM work. The complete main text, four figures, nine tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated-training experiments measuring safety, utility, efficiency, and malicious-update detection on Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, including Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds Qwen2.5-7B baseline comparisons in Appendix D.4, Table 9.

M1.justification: The LoRA-Probe design, Step-Level, Client-Level and Shadow-Level defenses, early freezing, round skipping, and security-weighted aggregation remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LMSYS-Chat/WildChat and BeaverTails/MaliciousGen pairings, AdvBench safety evaluation, MT-Bench first-turn utility evaluation, and malicious-client scenarios. The added baseline rows introduce no new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds DnC, FLAME, and LASA to the Qwen2.5-7B comparison across all four existing dataset pairings at 30% malicious participation. These methods were already evaluated on Llama3.1-8B in Table 2; the addition completes comparator coverage for the retained Qwen experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated probe-data exclusion from overlap with 'test sets' to overlap with 'model training data,' retaining the same first 4,000 benign and 2,500 malicious samples. This revises the reported split relationship without establishing resampling or reruns. Other previously stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The LoRA-separability visualization, malicious-client-ratio robustness results, detector analysis, and roundwise precision analysis are retained. The additional Table 9 benchmark comparisons introduce no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analytical question.

E5.justification: The initialization and seed-consistency discussion is unchanged. Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds results for three Qwen baselines. For BeaverTails & LMSYS-Chat, the newly reported Rule scores are 80.58 for DnC, 77.88 for FLAME, and 67.50 for LASA, alongside the retained Shadow-Level score of 97.88. All shared numerical entries and figure findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), feature normalization, security-weight definitions, and the two-stage sigmoid calibration retain the same mathematics. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of FedLLM vulnerability, separable benign/malicious LoRA updates, and effective low-overhead defense while preserving utility. The added comparisons support existing claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of update-distribution drift and shadow-branch stability are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning initialization consistency, probe transferability across backbones, and the computational cost of Shadow-Level.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies a maximum sequence length of 256. This adds reproducibility information without establishing a changed setting. The other disclosed hyperparameters, stabilization details, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. Changes to author lists, citation years, titles, venues, and page ranges are bibliographic metadata revisions, including the retained FLTrust, Kairouz, and Residual references.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits, a streamlined implementation paragraph, revised overlap wording, and bibliographic edits. The section order, appendix organization, and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 9 gains comparator rows and moves to a separate page. Tables 2, 3, and 9 replace broad boldface emphasis with selective highlighting of safety maxima, and several captions are revised. All four figure images remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 9 fills missing Qwen comparisons against DnC, FLAME, and LASA, making the cross-backbone evidence more complete. The newly documented sequence length and selective table highlighting improve reproducibility and readability. These gains are limited: shared results and limitations remain unchanged, and Appendix A's overlap revision does not establish that the underlying experiments changed.
